name: climate.countries

name: carbon.tipped
summary: The first cascade: a tipping element past its threshold releases the carbon its row of data/events/tipping.toml states, on the row's timescale, into the carbon ledger, where the pools module treats it as it treats fossil carbon, so the warming it adds comes back through the same energy balance. Three elements carry a carbon table from Armstrong McKay et al. 2022: boreal permafrost abrupt thaw (per degree, declining), Amazon partial dieback (30 GtC), boreal permafrost collapse (125 GtC). Each year the mass still owed is released as a first-order approach over the element's timescale. Nothing is modelled here; the amounts, thresholds and timescales are the assessment's and the module only moves the stated mass over the stated time.
dt: 1 year (1 January), after the tipping check

notes: The feedbacks with the other sign are left out on purpose and said so: the boreal forest's southern dieback releases carbon but its net effect in the assessment is cooling (a lighter surface), and its northern expansion takes carbon up but warms on net (a darker one); both are albedo terms this energy balance has no place for, so including only their carbon would be the wrong sign. Methane from thawing permafrost is folded into the assessment's CO2-equivalent and is not separately represented. The release is first-order on the stated timescale; the assessment gives a timescale, not a shape.

views.title: what this run does not yet measure
views.source: Not in this run, so not in these numbers: deaths from heat (a published exposure-response layer is next), harvests and food prices, biodiversity, fresh water, sea level from ice, migration, and any response by people to any of it. Of the tipping elements, only the carbon of permafrost and the Amazon feeds back, and only once the run passes the assessment's thresholds; the rest are flags. The population here is the UN's path, which assumes none of the above changes where people live. Every crossing above is a count of people living where a stated limit is passed, not a toll, and the model runs about 0.15 °C warm in 2024. The warming applied to a place is its country's, from the country record scaled by the run's global anomaly: wherever something has held a country's warming back so far, this holds it back still, and within a country the pattern of the recent past is held.

name: fire.rothermel
summary: A wildfire on real terrain: Rothermel's surface spread model on a one-arc-second DEM window, a fuel model per cell from WorldCover land cover, dead fuel moisture from the hour's humidity and temperature, wind speed and direction from the ERA5 archive at the window's centre; fire moves cell to cell down an ellipse headed along the wind-plus-slope vector. No suppression, no spotting, no crown fire; built-up land burns at a guessed rate the manifest can set to zero.
